implementation_notes: TypeScript inherits JavaScript's generator syntax, so a typed Generator<A> built from a seed plus a step function is the default realization, and the types make the emitted element and the state explicit. Where the step function should be a first-class value, fp-ts models the scheme as the Unfoldable type class with unfold instances for Array and Stream - (B, (b: B) => Option<[A, B]>) => HKT<F, A> - which keeps the stop condition in the Option type instead of a null sentinel. Tree unfolds remain recursive builders with explicit node types, because the language has no built-in lazy structure.
pitfalls: Generator's type parameters (Generator<A, TReturn, TNext>) must be spelled out when values are sent back into the generator, otherwise TNext infers as unknown.
The step function's type cannot enforce that the emitted value and the next state stay in step: a wrong next-state type only surfaces if the unfold is generic over the state parameter.
emit-downlevel settings (a target below ES2015, or downlevelIteration off) change what spreading a generator compiles to, so the same source can materialise eagerly.
